blocks.text: JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Jair. A Gileadite who judged twenty-two years; thirty sons on thirty ass colts.
LED ISRAELi
22 years No years BC in Scripture
TRIBE
Not stated (a Gileadite)
IN THE LINE
8th of 15
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“He had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havoth-jair…”

THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
THE CYCLE
Forgetting, oppression, a cry, a deliverer, rest
1 · FORGOT GOD Scripture does not say.

THE NATION
What the nation did
His thirty sons rode thirty ass colts and held thirty cities in Gilead. Judges 10:4
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
22 years of judging (Judges 10:3). No year BC is given.
Clans rather than individuals
Moore (1895)
Moore holds that most, if not all, of these names "appear to be those of clans rather than individuals", and that their years sit outside the book's chronological scheme.[20]
Individual judges over part of Israel
Keil (1865)
Keil treats them as judges in office one after another, and argues that Jephthah, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon were "not judges over all Israel".[1]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 4
Judges 10 Numbers 32 Deuteronomy 3 1 Chronicles 2
PASSAGES · 4
Judges 10:3–5 Numbers 32:41 Deuteronomy 3:14 1 Chronicles 2:22
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture names no enemy, battle, sin or rest for this judge: only the years judged, family and burial.
Judges does not name Jair's tribe; Gilead lay east of the Jordan.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textThe site keeps the judge separate from "Jair the son of Manasseh" of Moses' time (jair-num-32-41), who also named towns Havoth-jair. Numbers 32:41 Judges 10:4
